blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — enoxaparin reversal and protamine safety monitoring
stem: A client with serious bleeding after enoxaparin receives protamine sulfate. Which nursing interpretation is most accurate after the protamine is given?

options.A: Treat the protamine dose as complete reversal and stop focused bleeding surveillance because clinically meaningful enoxaparin anti-factor Xa activity should no longer remain.
options.B: Continue assessing bleeding and clinical response because protamine incompletely neutralizes enoxaparin anti-factor Xa activity, while also monitoring for severe hypotensive or anaphylactoid reactions.
options.C: Interpret persistent anticoagulant effect as evidence that protamine has no useful role in enoxaparin overdose and should not be used when serious bleeding is present.
options.D: Focus on recurrent thrombosis rather than protamine reactions because severe hypotension and anaphylactoid reactions are no longer relevant after protamine administration.

rationale: Current LOVENOX labeling states that protamine may largely neutralize enoxaparin, but anti-Factor Xa activity is never completely neutralized; maximal neutralization is about 60%. Ongoing assessment for bleeding and clinical response therefore remains necessary after protamine. The same section warns that protamine can cause severe hypotensive and anaphylactoid reactions and that fatal anaphylaxis-like reactions have occurred, so appropriate monitoring and resuscitation capability remain important. Therefore B is correct. A falsely assumes complete reversal, C incorrectly says protamine has no useful role, and D dismisses a serious protamine safety risk.
educational_objective: Recognize that protamine provides incomplete reversal of enoxaparin anti-Factor Xa activity and that continued bleeding assessment plus monitoring for severe protamine reactions remains necessary.

source_claim_supported: Protamine incompletely reverses enoxaparin anti-Factor Xa activity (maximum about 60% neutralization) and can itself cause severe hypotensive or anaphylactoid reactions, requiring continued clinical surveillance.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as substantive post-reversal interpretations of comparable length.
Removed absolute-word cueing and retained the directly sourced incomplete anti-Xa neutralization and protamine reaction risks.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B uniquely reflects LOVENOX §10: reversal is incomplete and protamine itself carries severe reaction risk.
